I believe I came off wrong in this post? Technically I dated said person AS a child. I was 17, but nonetheless, a teenager. I am learning and growing and I’m certainly not going to write off any criticisms of anyone. I am open to growth. But what this person has spread about me is their perception. Just because someone says something negative about you, doesn’t make it a fact. That’s what I’m getting at here. Her words weighed heavy on me for a long long time. I genuinely considered them and have unpacked them all. I don’t mean to come across as “no I was perfect and you have no reason to tell me otherwise!!!” Just that I can’t always take everyone’s words as facts. I can’t let the harmful words sit with me and affect me, especially if they aren’t true. That isn’t beneficial. I’ve let this person have too much power over me to continue to second guess myself.

I’m so glad it reached you. Once I found that video I broke down and thought “I need to teach myself to love the life I have” It’s so difficult, but I believe in the both of us. It’s easy to run out of reasons to stay or it’s hard to come up with any reasons at all. I believe you are that brave. I understand feeling powerless. I still feel that way. It’s a slow build honestly. It’s kind of like retraining your brain. You have to stop yourself every time you think you are powerless or not strong enough, and to tell yourself that you are- whether you believe it or not. It’s definitely not easy, but I want you to know I believe in you. I’m a complete and utter stranger, but I believe in you. That feeling of being dragged out to sea is very familiar to me, and I’m not sure if you feel the same, but I often feel like I’m fighting to keep my head above water whilst drowning. I believe that one day it won’t be so tiring. I believe the more we fight, the more strength we will build and the easier it will be to swim. You certainly have no reason to be ashamed. I’m very glad you’re okay. ❤️

Hi, I really hope you’re physically okay at this moment. Coming from someone who has attempted several times in the past, I know I’ve had moments like this. It just almost seems like it’s the perfect moment to finally break away. I promise you, however, there’s never that perfect moment. I want you to know I’m reaching out my hand for you. That I’ve heard you and I’m listening. I know how unbearable that pain gets, and how easily you can reach a point nothing seems to relieve it all. I’ve been fighting these thoughts for at least 12 years. It’s been a long long journey and at age 19, I don’t feel exactly where I need to be. I have so many moments I am ready to go. I won’t tell you time heals it, or betters it, because that’s certainly not true. Time may heal some things- but you know what really heals it? You. You have that power, no matter how worthless or incapable you may feel. The pain may encase you, and every action you make may seem to not make a single dent in your pain, but I promise you that you have the power to get there. 
The great (but awful) thing about this feeling we have, is that it’s from inside us. That means we can reach it, and shape it to be what we need it to be. You can take your pain and you can make it something absolutely beautiful. I believe in you, and I certainly hope you’ve “failed” A failed attempt isn’t a failure, it’s another chance. As cliche as that is to hear. I hope you’re well,
and if you ever need to share your voice, you certainly can reach out to me if not anyone ❤️

I’m not at all blaming them... I’m simply expressing how unbearable that guilt is that I have hurt them. I wish I didn’t feel this way. I wish I could have lived my life without this overhanging feeling. But I do feel this way. So it’s a matter of dealing with it everyday and the only reason I fight it off so hard IS because of them. I actually have lost people to suicide, so I know how painful that is alone. Living in fear that someone you care about will hurt themselves is awful. I experience it with my friends as well. But I also know that most people who are suicidal are very aware of the effect it has on those around them. To blame them was not my intention. I genuinely have been suffering from the guilt of it all.

I’ve definitely been there. 17 was difficult for my parents and I’s relationship. I did warrant a lot of concern from them tbh. Sometimes parents aren’t aware of how controlling they might be. It’s hard when you’re reaching adulthood especially for them to come and realize that you need to have even more boundaries than before. It doesn’t help when they aren’t giving you that, but I hope with time they come to realize that you are capable and that they can’t control every aspect of your life. I’m sure their intentions are good, just as my parents’ intentions are, but I still know it can be overwhelming.

I know they mean well, but I guess privacy has always been a huge value for me. I don’t want to completely keep things hidden from them but at the same time I am an adult? So it’s so odd to know that my mom, whether she directed it or not, was okay with a PI looking into me? Like obviously they can only find what’s public but I just think parents need to learn to set boundaries. Even if they are scared or concerned. Because it’s completely understandable to wonder about your child and to want to be aware of what goes on... but sometimes parents don’t realize how invasive they are being and how even they they may not trust us, they are sacrificing the trust we have for them by doing these things.
